title: Nocturne inference todo + scratch
content:
2026-03-13 (late) - quick scratchpad / action list

Context: after the 02:15 deploy we saw intermittent p99 regressions (~300–700ms extra) for short seq (<128) text gen routes. Appears correlated with KV-cache warmup and occasional RVAP deadlock in cache manager (logs show the same thread waiting for kv-lock while another thread is blocked on nvlink transfer). Seen on two machines (gpu-node-21, gpu-node-24).

Observed symptoms:
- p99 spikes on text-gen-route A (seq < 128) at 02:20, 02:36, 03:01 (matches autoscaler bursts).
- Stacktrace snippet (from journalctl):
  - kv_cache_manager.cpp: acquire_kv_mutex -> block -> waiting on nvlink_transfer_cv
  - nvlink driver shows transient queue_full errors around same timestamps
- GPU util vs token throughput mismatch (gpu_util 90% but tokens/s lower than expected) -> suggests blocking on transfers not compute.

Quick repro steps I ran (notes):
- reproduced locally on staging with small batch flood: ab -n 500 -c 50 against /v1/generate?model=redwood-lite (seq=64) -> saw 220ms->600ms tail.
- captured runtime trace with perf_event (light): perf record -g -F 99 -o /tmp/perf.data && perf script | FlameGraph
- collected /proc/driver/nvlink and nvidia-smi dmon for 5m window; nvlink queue_full spikes line up with p99 spikes.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache eviction + async prefetch triggers nvlink transfers that saturate limited link buffer -> other threads block waiting for transfers to finish -> p99. (most likely)
2) A race between cache manager's mutex and the transfer completion callback leading to a temporary deadlock. (possible; stacktraces hint)
3) Kernel-level driver bug triggered by bursty small batches sequence length distribution (less likely but keep in mind).

Immediate mitigation options (fast, ordered):
- [P0] Add short-term guard: throttle async prefetches to 4 concurrent transfers for routes tagged small-seq. (low-risk config flip)
- [P1] Fall back to CPU copy path for nodes that report nvlink errors in the last 10m. (requires small runtime toggle)
- [P2] Disable prefix prefetch for canary group (5% traffic) and monitor p99.

Things to try tomorrow (experiments):
- Experiment A: limit concurrent nvlink transfers per GPU (via runtime flag --max-nvlink-transfers=4). Measure p50/p95/p99 and GPU util.
- Experiment B: change eviction policy to LRU-approx with fast-path eviction for very small prefixes to reduce number of prefetches.
- Experiment C: increase nvlink buffer allocation in kernel config (coordinate with infra and hardware team) if we can replicate on more machines.

Data we need to gather:
- token-level latency traces mapped to transfer start/finish timestamps (add a tiny tracing span around transfer calls).
- per-node nvlink error counters + syslog around spike windows.
- inspect commit range for last deploy (PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4872) for changes to prefetch logic.

Short TODOs (me):
- [ ] Add --max-nvlink-transfers flag to local runtime (prototype branch) and smoke test on staging (ETA: morning)
- [ ] Wire a tiny transfer span in tracer (2cp + unit test) so we can graph transfer durations separately (ETA: today am)
- [ ] Create canary rollout plan to disable prefix prefetch on 5% traffic (write steps & rollback) (ETA: today)
- [ ] Post summary in #runtime-oncall with hypothesis and ask HW folks about recent nvlink driver updates (Jun loop in)
- [ ] If mitigations help, make follow-up ticket to revisit eviction strategy with perf numbers (RINF-2145 follow-up)

Open questions / notes to self:
- Are we sure prefetch happens for tiny sequence lengths? Need to confirm logic in prefetch planner (check code path planner::should_prefetch(seq_len)).
- Check whether autoscaler burst policy correlates — maybe scale-up triggers many new workers which each prefetch, amplifying transfers. If so, consider staggering prefetch during scale-up.
- If we throttle prefetch, measure extra cold-token penalty vs p99 improvement (tradeoff).

Commands / quick snippets: (paste into shell)
- tail -n 500 /var/log/serving/runtime.log | grep "nvlink" --color
- sudo cat /proc/driver/nvlink | grep queue_full
- ab -n 500 -c 50 "http://staging.internal/v1/generate?model=redwood-lite&seq=64"
- ./bin/runtime --max-nvlink-transfers=4 --route-tag=small-seq --trace-transfers=1

Slack/PRs to check: 
- PR 4872 (prefetch rework) -> code owner: @jun-park
- Runtime oncall convo 03/13 03:40 in #runtime-oncall -> thread link in linked_artifacts

Evening wrap: prioritize the flag prototype tomorrow morning, try canary rollback plan if prototype reduces spikes. If no improvement, escalate to HW drivers team and open ticket with nvlink logs + perf flame.

Random brain dump (don’t forget):
- Maybe adapt prefetch to be size-aware: only prefetch when expected token horizon > 256 for that batch. Could reduce small-seq amplification.
- Consider a soft-queue for transfer requests so the transfer thread can schedule smarter (fairness across routes).

End of scratchpad.
